jobs.title: Processing Lab Technician
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The lab technician is responsible for maintaining processing tanks and the batch treatment area in compliance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulations. The lab tech uses lab equipment to prepare reagents and solutions, troubleshoot lab and test‑related problems, and review test results to ensure standards are met. Typical duties also include measuring levels, pH, and other chemical composition; coordinating and performing chemical adjustments and tank cleaning in accordance with safety procedures, internal work processes, and applicable regulations. This position is classified as safety‑sensitive.

This role is identified as requiring ITAR compliance; qualified candidates must meet the definition of a U.S. Person (per EAR Part 772 and ITAR 120.15):

• An individual who is granted U.S. citizenship

• An individual who is granted U.S. permanent residence (Green Card holder)

• An individual who is granted status as a "protected person"

Essential Functions

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities.

• Maintains processing tanks and batch treatment area per established procedures and regulatory standards; performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks as appropriate

• Prepares lab reagents/solutions

• Maintains and operates lab equipment, including pipettes, burettes, TDS, and pH meters; troubleshoots basic lab and test‑related issues; ensures proper use, care, and storage of equipment

• Performs "Adds", "Decant", "Builds" and "Drops" of processing tanks

• Completes accurate, timely, and legible quality records in accordance with AS9100 Quality Policy and NADCAP requirements; inputs QC data into the information management system

• Completes regulatory and hazardous waste reporting and disposal records as required

• Coordinates with internal/external sources for preventative maintenance schedules on all lab equipment

• Maintains quality procedures, quality assurance instructions, and process control procedures to conform to all applicable customer requirements, industry standards, and registration systems; supports and participates as needed in AS/ISO/Nadcap/customer/supplier quality audits of process and products

• Assists in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance quality, productivity, and cost‑effectiveness based on observations and experience; provides technical expertise and works with operators to identify and implement improvements to reduce waste and improve efficiency; implements lean principles, techniques, and methods as appropriate

Work Experience

• Minimum of 1 year experience in a quality role in a manufacturing environment is required

• Experience in continuous improvement concepts such as Six Sigma and Lean is preferred

• Knowledge of and experience with the requirements of AS9100

jobs.title: Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman (Oil & Gas Manufacturing)
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Electrical & Instrumentation Journeyman Level II to support the build, wiring, testing, and commissioning of oil & gas measurement equipment, including meter tubes, ultrasonic meter runs, orifice systems, sample systems, and packaged measurement skids. This role is ideal for a technician with strong electrical fundamentals and hands-on instrumentation experience who can work independently in a manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
• Install, wire, and terminate electrical and instrumentation components for:
• * Ultrasonic, turbine, and orifice meter systems
• Flow computers, transmitters, and RTDs
• Sample systems, analyzers, and probe assemblies
• Control panels, junction boxes, and skid-mounted I&E systems
• Perform conduit routing, cable tray installation, cable pulls, and panel terminations according to shop standards.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, P&IDs, and measurement drawings.
• Assist in the build and testing of measurement skids, including powering up systems, verifying signals, and supporting FAT procedures.
• Troubleshoot electrical and instrumentation issues using multimeters, loop calibrators, and diagnostic tools.
• Support measurement PM’s and drafting teams with redlines, revisions, and technical feedback.
• Document work performed, materials used, and test results for QA and traceability.

Required Qualifications
• Valid Journeyman Electrician License (state-issued).
• 2–3 years of electrical experience.
• Working knowledge of instrumentation, including transmitters, flow computers, RTDs, solenoids, and control wiring.
• Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, and measurement schematics.
• Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, and electrical test equipment.
• Ability to lift 50+ lbs, work in fabrication environments, and perform physically demanding tasks.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to measurement accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working in fabrication, skid manufacturing, or with oil & gas equipment.
• Experience wiring PLC/VFD panels, motor controls, and low-voltage control systems.
• Knowledge of hazardous area classifications and wiring methods (Class I Div 1/2).
• Experience supporting FAT testing, signal verification, and commissioning.

jobs.title: Calibration Technician
jobs.description:
## Calibration Technician – Precision Measurement Expert

We are seeking a highly skilled Calibration Technician to join our team at Cherokee Nation Government Solutions, a part of Cherokee Federal. This role is a subject matter expert in various calibration disciplines, working with multifunctional and interrelated precision measurement equipment, instruments, and instrumentation systems using electrical, electronic, physical, dimensional, and optical standards. You will support technical assessments and recommend measurement solutions, often unique in design or system configuration.

This position supports Department of Defense (DoD) production and maintenance operations, requiring adherence to applicable government, industry, and corporate procedures. A government contract requires that this position be restricted to U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents; you must provide documentation of your status.

### Compensation & Benefits

Estimated starting salary range: **$32–$35 per hour**, commensurate with experience. Full-time benefits include Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K, and other possible benefits as provided (subject to change without notice).

### What You’ll Do

- Apply metrology principles to calibrate a wide array of precision measurement instruments, systems, and standards – including pulse generators, frequency counters, voltmeters, optical time-domain reflectometers, dimensional measurement devices, and electro-optic test systems.

- Set up and operate calibration equipment under actual or simulated conditions, using physical dimensional reference standards to ensure traceability.

- Establish appropriate measurement tolerances based on equipment specifications.

- Systematically identify calibration issues, define root causes, and evaluate alternative corrective actions.

- Calculate test uncertainty and test uncertainty ratio (TUR) to confirm suitability of calibration standards; document measurement uncertainty per national and international standards.

- Use computer programming routines to configure and adjust equipment operating parameters.

- Deliver work that meets quality standards and complete assignments within established timelines.

- Troubleshoot and repair new systems during operational testing; refine procedures to address unforeseen defects.

- Operate and maintain equipment safely, following all safety rules and regulations.

- Draft and submit changes to detailed schematics, drawings, and maintenance procedures for approval and use by junior personnel.

- Document software applications and modifications; submit all documentation to the Configuration/Data Management (C/DM) office.

- Test and debug programs to detailed requirements; submit completed application software to the C/DM office.

- Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, and/or hydraulic principles.

- Exercise sound judgment and independence in selecting methods and techniques to resolve complex calibration challenges.

- Perform other duties as assigned.

### Key Systems and Equipment

You’ll work with equipment such as multimeters and calibrators, torque wrenches and transducers, pressure gauges, dead weight testers, vacuum gauges, oscilloscopes, thread gauges, pin sets, and optical comparators.

### Core Technical Tasks

These tasks are highly procedure-driven, documentation-heavy, and require meticulous attention to detail – a single incorrect calibration can deadline equipment or take weapons systems offline:

- Perform Precision Calibration

- Troubleshoot and Repair TMDE

- Calculate and Document Measurement Uncertainty

- Precision Alignment and Adjustment

- Verify and Maintain Laboratory Reference Standards

- Operate Automated Calibration Systems

- Conduct Out-of-Tolerance (OOT) Inspections

- Environmental Monitoring and Control

- Calibrate and Certify Automated Test Equipment (ATE)

- Quality Assurance and Internal Audits

- Customer Interface and Training

About the Opportunity

The Scientific Programmer II bridges the gap between scientific development and operational production by integrating, testing, validating, and supporting scientific software applications in a remote work environment. This role collaborates with Science Teams, developers, and stakeholders to document requirements, establish test baselines, verify outputs, and ensure code changes are successfully transitioned into reliable operational environments.

Success is demonstrated through accurate integrations, effective stakeholder coordination, high-quality testing and documentation, and the delivery of dependable production-ready solutions.

What You Will Do in This Role

The Scientific Programmer II supports the integration, testing, validation, and operational deployment of scientific software and algorithms, ensuring accurate, reliable, and production-ready solutions.

• Understand and document algorithm inputs, outputs, and production rules across all units, including how requirements differ between units, to ensure accurate implementation and operational consistency.

• Define operational run procedures, including run triggers, intermediate file handoffs, and final delivered output products to support reliable and repeatable production processing.

• Establish and maintain a baseline test case for each project; create one when the Science Team does not provide it, and validate it with them to ensure scientific and operational accuracy.

• Compare all future code updates and changes against the established baseline to assess impacts, validate expected behavior, and maintain system integrity.

• Review regression testing results as applicable and identify, document, and resolve discrepancies affecting algorithm performance or output quality.

• Communicate progress and issues across stakeholders, including tracking tasks in Jira and coordinating with the Science Team and other stakeholders to support project execution and operational readiness.

• Integrate code in accordance with established coding standards, interface modules, and build scripts; perform static compilation and complete required project checklists to ensure successful deployment into operational environments.

• Verify output file accuracy and standards compliance, including format and logging requirements, to ensure data quality and adherence to project specifications.

• Demo code and production rules at delivery, and provide ongoing guidance and support during transition to facilitate successful adoption and operational handoff.

• Test against upstream input changes and provide test cases to support downstream algorithm changes, ensuring continued compatibility across interconnected systems and workflows.

• Participate in code reviews across projects to promote code quality, maintainability, adherence to standards, and knowledge sharing among team members.

What You Will Bring

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related scientific or technical discipline.

• 4–6 years of experience supporting scientific software, system integration, software deployment, testing, validation, or operational environments.

• Hands-on experience with FORTRAN, C, or C++ for scientific application support, integration, maintenance, or performance-focused development.

• Working knowledge of Python for automation, scripting, testing, or application support activities.

• Strong understanding of software integration principles, configuration management, APIs, interfaces, data flows, and production processing workflows.

Your Job
Georgia Pacific's Consumer Products Group is seeking candidates for an Electrical and Instrumentation (E & I) Technician opportunity supporting our Muskogee, OK Tissue, Towel, and Napkin Mill. This individual will work with supervisors, mentors, coworkers, and others to gain knowledge and skills in our manufacturing environment and to ensure that the electrical and mechanical needs of the mill can be met. The pay range will be $26.00 - $38.86 based on experience. The shift will be 12-hour rotating shift or a Day shift depending on need and to include holidays, weekends and overtime as needed.

$2500 sign on bonus!

Our Team

Located on the Kerr-McClellan Navigational Channel (Arkansas River) on about 640 acres of land, the Muskogee consumer products operation spans across approximately 70 acres (or 2,900,000 square feet) of manufacturing and warehouse space are "under roof" employing approximately 830 employees. We are the second largest employer in the Muskogee, OK area and 45th in the state! Our non-union facility operates on 12-hour shifts, 7 days per week, 365 days per year. The site housing 2 of the 13 largest tissue machines in the world and paper machines that produce an average of 900 tons of paper per day. Our finished product consists of a mix of 40% Retail and 60% Commercial.
